Placeholder/What's Fake: ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-06 for user-reported 'report count flashes to the right number then back to 0'. All four Firestore addSnapshotListener callbacks discarded the error parameter and treated snapshot==null the same as 'zero documents' (snapshot?.documents.orEmpty()). Firestore actually calls the listener with snapshot=null on TRANSIENT errors (a listen-stream reconnect, a brief DNS/network blip like the one seen in this session's Logcat) - often moments before delivering a fresh, correct snapshot right after. That null-as-empty behavior meant a real 'this device had a one-second network hiccup' event visibly reset the UI's report count and list to empty before recovering, which is exactly the flash the user saw.
What You Need To Do: FIXED - all four listeners now check the error parameter explicitly (log + record via CrashReporter and return without emitting) and only trySend when snapshot is genuinely non-null. Area: App re-asking for login credentials every reopen
Placeholder/What's Fake: ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-09 for user-reported "the app should keep asking to login after exiting every time, only ask for creds if the user sign out" (i.e. it currently DOES ask every time, which is wrong - Firebase Auth already persists a signed-in session across app restarts on its own). RootNavGraph's one-time startGraph decision (`remember { ... isLoggedIn -> MAIN_GRAPH else -> AUTH_GRAPH }`) is deliberately snapshotted only ONCE on first composition (see its own doc comment - re-deriving it live would tear down AUTH_GRAPH's back stack mid-registration). But isLoggedIn was fed from `authRepository.currentUser.collectAsState(initial = null)`, and collectAsState's `initial` value has no way to distinguish "the flow hasn't emitted yet" from "it emitted null" - both looked identically like isLoggedIn == false on that very first composition, which is BEFORE Firebase's real AuthStateListener callback has had a chance to fire even when a valid persisted session exists. So the one-time decision was made using a placeholder value, not the real auth state, on literally every cold start - sending an already-logged-in user back to the login screen every single time, regardless of Remember Me or any actual sign-out.
What You Need To Do: FIXED - added a hasKnownAuthState flag (flips true only once currentUser's flow has genuinely emitted at least once, via a .onEach{} side effect) and changed RootNavGraph's isLoggedIn parameter to Boolean? (null == "not yet known", distinct from "known signed out"). RootNavGraph now simply doesn't compose the NavHost at all (`if (isLoggedIn == null) return`) until the real auth state has arrived, so the one-time startGraph snapshot is only ever taken with the CORRECT value. Signing out (AuthRepository.logout()) still correctly routes to AUTH_GRAPH via the existing explicit onLoggedOut navigate() call, unaffected by this fix. Verified with compileDebugKotlin; needs real-device retest specifically closing/reopening the app (not just backgrounding) while signed in, since that's the exact path this bug lived on.

Area: Enable-biometric popup did not require an actual biometric scan
Placeholder/What's Fake: CHANGED 2026-09-09 per explicit request ("it should ask the user to input the biometric like fingerprint or face rec"). Previously, tapping "Enable" on the post-login popup called BiometricCredentialStore.enable() directly from the button's onClick - biometric login could be switched on with a tap alone, no fingerprint/face scan ever required at enable time (only later, at actual sign-in, did BiometricPrompt ever appear). Split into two steps: tapping Enable now only sets a pendingBiometricEnableChallenge flag; LoginScreen reacts to that by launching a real BiometricPrompt.authenticate() challenge (no CryptoObject needed here, since encryption - unlike decryption - isn't Keystore-gated, see BiometricCredentialStore's own doc comment), and BiometricCredentialStore.enable() is now only ever called from that prompt's onAuthenticationSucceeded callback.

Area: Biometric hardware/enrollment must already exist on the device - report talking point
Placeholder/What's Fake: DOCUMENTED 2026-09-09 per explicit user request ("they should already exist on the device first, write this in placeholder, it will be an interesting point to report on"). This was already true before today's change and required no code fix - BiometricAuthManager.isAvailable() calls BiometricManager.canAuthenticate(BIOMETRIC_STRONG) and only returns true when the device BOTH has usable biometric-class-strong hardware AND the user has actually enrolled at least one fingerprint/face. Every entry point that can show a biometric prompt or offer to enable biometric login (LoginScreen's post-login popup, the Sign in with biometrics button, Settings' toggle) checks this first and simply doesn't offer the feature at all when it's false - there is no separate "biometrics unavailable" error state to hit, the option is just absent. unavailableReason() exists purely to explain WHY (no hardware / hardware temporarily unavailable / nothing enrolled yet) for a settings-screen hint, distinguishing three different real-world causes rather than one generic message. Worth including in the report as a deliberate defense-in-depth design point: the app never attempts to gate a real security decision (turning on biometric login) behind hardware it hasn't first confirmed can actually authenticate the user.
